LESSON: VISUAL DISCRIMINATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.1: Visual discrimination
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Visual discrimination, part of Reading in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we use different items and objects found at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize pictures of things found at home, ● Read pictures of things found at home such as people, animals, houses, farm tools, furniture, utensils, digital devices, clothes 1. How do we use different items and objects found at home? 41

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual discrimination in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. points out similarities and differences in pictures of objects found at home,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual discrimination in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. point out differences in pictures of objects found at home,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual discrimination in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. enjoy observing things in the environment for details. . and plants either from a video clip, books, cards, charts or board. Learners with speech difficulties to read audio books or point at the pictures as others read. ● Identify similarities and differences in the pictures on their use, where they are found, colour, and size among other factors. ● Identify differences in the pictures on their use, where they are found, color, size among other factors, ● Look at the things found in the class and relate them to some things found at home for example, tables, desks and furniture at home, buildings, plants, toilets among others, ● Talk about things in school and not at home as well as things at home and not in school like animals and farm tools, ● Engage in games where they 2. How do we take care of the things found at home? 42 jump while in a circle when anything found at home is mentioned but remain still if what is mentioned is not found at home. Learners with mobility devices can raise their hands or clap /tap when anything found at home is mentioned. ● Sing songs related to things found at home. Learners with speech difficulties could hum, mime tap, clap or move with the rhythm of the song.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual discrimination in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Visual discrimination together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● .Self- efficacy what is home and school as the learner looks at the things found in the class and relate them to some things

found at home for example, tables, desks and furniture at home, buildings, plants, toilets among others,

● Digital literacy and technological awareness interacting with digital technology as the learner is guided by the teacher to

identify things found at home from digital devices.

Values:
● Love is enhanced as the learner puts the interest of others before their own as they learn together and appreciate other

learners’ views while reading about things found at home.

● Responsibility is enhanced as the learner identifies ways of taking care of furniture and utensils among other things found at

home.

43

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Disaster Risk Reduction is enhanced as the learner is cautioned against some harmful things found at home.

Link to other Learning Areas: Mathematics as learners are involved in checking what is more and less.

Suggested learning resources: Tables, desks and furniture, buildings, plants, toilets ,video clip, books, cards, charts or board,

pictures on farm tools
